definitions.explanation: a container or utensil used for serving or drinking sake or other alcoholic beverages

examples.japanese: {美|うつく}しい{酒器|しゅき}を{集|あつ}める。
この{酒器|しゅき}は{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}のものです。
examples.english: This sake vessel is from the Edo period.

examples.japanese: {陶芸|とうげい}{教室|きょうしつ}で{自分|じぶん}だけの{酒器|しゅき}を{作|つく}ってみませんか。
examples.english: Why not try making your own sake vessel in a pottery class?

notes:
A general term for vessels used to serve and drink sake. Japanese sake culture places great importance on the aesthetic and material qualities of drinking vessels, and choosing the right {酒器|しゅき} is considered part of the sake-drinking experience.

TYPES:
- {徳利|とっくり} — sake carafe/flask (for warming and pouring)
- {猪口|ちょこ} / お{猪口|ちょこ} — small sake cup
- {杯|さかずき} — flat ceremonial sake cup
- {枡|ます} — square wooden sake cup
- {片口|かたくち} — single-spouted pouring vessel

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {酒器|しゅき}セット — sake set (flask and cups together)
- {陶器|とうき}の{酒器|しゅき} — ceramic sake vessel
- {錫|すず}の{酒器|しゅき} — tin/pewter sake vessel
- {酒器|しゅき}{選|えら}び — choosing a sake vessel

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditional etiquette calls for pouring sake for others rather than for oneself ({お酌|しゃく}). The shape, material, and size of the vessel affect how sake is experienced — wide-mouthed cups release more aroma, while narrow ones concentrate it.
